To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CSF1 induces the expression of the Tie2 receptor on CD14+ human and mouse monocytes and enhances their migratory response to ANG2, a process that requires Tie2 receptor signaling.
CSF1 augments Tie2-expressing monocyte differentiation, angiogenic function, and recruitment in a mouse model of breast cancer.
CSF1 treatment increases CD14+/TIE2+ cells in breast cancer, which results in an increased angiogenic phenotype and tumor growth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanism behind CSF1-induced differentiation of Tie2-expressing monocytes and their angiogenic function.
understanding the role of CSF1 and Tie2 receptor-expressing macrophages in the breast tumor microenvironment.
the role of CSF1 on Tie2-expressing monocytes in breast cancer progression and the potential of these cells as a therapeutic target in breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

M-CSF is an important regulator of Tie2-expressing monocytes and that this population of cells can be recruited to sites of inflammation and tumor growth, and may contribute to the angiogenic response.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CSF1 is an important factor in the regulation of Tie2 receptor expression on a subset of monocytes and that CSF1-stimulation of this receptor can augment their angiogenic potential.

CSF1 augments Tie2 receptor expression on monocytes, which in turn enhances their migratory response to angiopoetin-2 and their angiogenic potential, and that this process is mediated by the PI3K and HIF pathways.
CSF1 can augment the Tie2 receptor on CD14+ TEMs, which results in an increased migratory response to ANG2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CSF1 can regulate the differentiation of CD14+ cells to the Tie2+ phenotype, which may have important implications for breast cancer progression.
CSF1 can regulate the differentiation and angiogenic potential of CD14+/TIE2+ cells.
CSF1 can induce Tie2 expression on monocytes in vitro and in vivo, and that Tie2-expressing monocytes can be recruited to the tumor microenvironment by CSF1.
